flags: The two NCDOT cache files contain identical guide excerpts ending in the Flat Rock chapter, before US 421. Their table of contents confirms the named route but not its specific scenic rationale, endpoints or length. Intro kept short because route-specific description is limited.

Dropped current claims of an 8.5-mile ascent, a native-stone-faced Parkway bridge, Snake Mountain and Elk Knob views, hardwood/mixed forest and horse/cattle farms: not present in cache. Christmas tree farms moment removed because no cache text supports the farms, Fraser fir or national production ranking.

Retained South Fork New River title with a short supported watershed account. Dropped the terminal bridge location, northward flow and second-oldest-river comparison, which the cache does not establish. Its placement after Deep Gap represents the adjacent headwaters, not a verified bridge stop.
Boone is the supported destination and new town moment, not a claim that the scenic designation extends through downtown. No strip towns or mileage were supplied.
Current Doc nickname story now attributed to Watson’s Legacy recording as the source does.

Cache/12.txt’s introduction says the 1931 route replaced NC 60 between Greensboro and Boone; its history says initial overlap from Winston-Salem and removal of NC 60 in 1934. Narrative uses the shared Boone endpoint and explicit overlap chronology, omitting the disputed eastern endpoint.
